rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance that all 10 compounds elute and reveal the overall retention window. This gives a first map of where the difficult pairs sit before optimizing slope, range, and temperature.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing analysis time. Keep composition and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient one step to test how much time can be removed before the weakest pair begins to lose resolution.

The 16 min gradient is nearly optimal on time and the limiting pair still has a little margin above 1.5. Reduce tG by one more step to try to bring the last peak under 10 min while checking whether pair 6/7 stays at full-credit resolution.

At 14 min the last peak is already within 10 min, so the remaining improvement must come from restoring the single weak pair without giving back much time. Narrow the gradient slightly at the top end to reduce gradient strength around the late cluster and hopefully increase selectivity/resolution for pair 6/7 while keeping the run fast.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue in the same direction. A further small reduction in phi1 may push that pair to full resolution with only a modest increase in retention.

Now that phi1 = 0.85 gave full resolution but slightly overshot the 10 min target, test whether shortening the gradient at the better-selectivity setting can recover time while preserving enough resolution. This directly probes whether a faster method near the current optimum can beat the 14 min, phi1 = 0.90 run.

The key tradeoff is clear: shorter tG hurts pair 6/7, while lower phi1 improves it. Test the crossed condition at 12 min with phi1 = 0.85 to see whether the gain in selectivity can restore full or near-full resolution while keeping the last peak closer to 10 min than at 14 min.

The best region is around phi1 = 0.90 and tG = 14 min, with only pair 6/7 limiting the score. Change temperature one step lower to probe whether selectivity for that pair improves enough to reach R >= 1.5 while keeping the last peak near 10 min.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction from the current best method. A modest increase to 45 C may improve the critical mid-run cluster enough to bring the weakest pair to full resolution while preserving a sub-10 min last peak.

Temperature shifts were strongly unfavorable, so stay at 40 C and now test a slightly shallower, slightly longer gradient around the best-selectivity composition. This should increase resolution of the limiting pair beyond the 14 min methods while potentially keeping the time penalty small enough to improve on the current best CRF.

We have mapped tG, phi1, and temperature; the remaining unexplored lever is the starting composition. Raising phi0 one step may reshape the early-to-mid gradient segment and improve the crowded 5–7 peak cluster without pushing the last peak past 10 min too severely.

Raising phi0 improved the critical pair while keeping t_last comfortably under 10 min, so combine that gain with the earlier beneficial effect of lowering phi1. This is the most promising nearby condition to push pair 6/7 above 1.5 and reach the maximum CRF.

A perfect CRF has been reached, so the only remaining objective is to see whether the method can be made faster without losing full-credit resolution. Shorten tG one step while keeping the successful composition and temperature fixed to test whether 1.000 can be retained with a shorter run.

The 12 min version lost too much resolution, so stay at 14 min and probe whether a slightly lower phi1 can preserve full resolution while pulling the successful operating point onto the safer side of the cliff. This checks whether the perfect method can be made more robust near the critical pair.

Injection 12 is perfect but sits essentially on the 10 min boundary, so test whether increasing phi0 one more step can trim the late retention while retaining the strong selectivity at phi1 = 0.85. This is a focused robustness check around the current optimum.

Injection 15 keeps perfect resolution with more time margin than injection 12, so push phi0 one more step higher to see if the method can be made even faster while staying fully resolved. This tests the edge of the optimum in the only direction that previously improved both robustness and retention time.

The optimum appears to sit between phi0 = 0.10–0.15 and phi1 = 0.85–0.90, with phi0 = 0.20 already too aggressive. Test phi0 = 0.15 with the slightly stronger upper composition to map the ridge around the perfect method and confirm whether injection 15 is the more robust optimum.

Injection 15 is perfect, and the surrounding tests suggest phi0 = 0.15 is favorable while phi1 controls the resolution/time balance. Testing phi1 = 0.80 will check whether the same full resolution can be retained with extra safety on the critical pair, or whether the time penalty becomes too large.

With two perfect methods already found, use remaining budget to map robustness around the best composition. Extending tG at the injection 15 composition should confirm the resolution reserve and quantify how steeply time penalty grows on the shallow side of the optimum.

The composition optimum is well established, so use remaining runs to test robustness to temperature around the best method. A +5 C change will show whether the perfect method is temperature-sensitive near the critical pair or remains broadly acceptable.

The +5 C test showed strong temperature sensitivity, so probe the other side of the optimum with a -5 C change at the best composition. This completes the local robustness map around the best method and confirms whether 40 C is uniquely favorable.

40 C is clearly optimal, and with the best method established the remaining useful question is whether a different composition can support a shorter gradient without losing too much on the critical pair. Phi1 = 0.80 gave the strongest resolution reserve near phi0 = 0.15, so pair it with tG = 12 to test the fastest plausible nearby alternative.

To use the last few runs efficiently, test the neighboring fast condition with lower phi0, since phi0 = 0.10 and phi1 = 0.85 previously gave stronger resolution than phi0 = 0.15 at shorter tG. This will check whether a different balance of start and end composition can rescue full resolution at 12 min.

With the optimum already secured, use the penultimate run to define the upper phi0 boundary at the best phi1/tG/T setting. This confirms how quickly the critical pair collapses beyond the successful phi0 = 0.15 condition and completes the local map.

Use the final run to bracket the full temperature range at the best composition and confirm how uniquely favorable 40 C is, since both 35 C and 45 C degraded selectivity. This last check adds robustness information without risking the campaign best, which is already at the maximum CRF.
